To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the proposed adaptive narrowband interference cancellation technique is effective in removing narrowband interference in CDMA systems; (2) the proposed technique is robust to the presence of other narrowband interferers and to changes in the narrowband interference; (3) the proposed technique does not require knowledge of the number or location of the narrowband interferers; and (4) the proposed technique requires only one adaptive weight for each narrowband interferer, as compared to a transversel filter,

(i) the proposed algorithm outperforms the transversal lters, in terms of both interference cancellation and desired signal distortion, and (ii) the proposed algorithm is able to remove interference which is not present in the training sequence used to adapt the receiver.
the proposed adaptive narrowband interference cancellation technique is able to reduce interference by 15dB in a 1/2 chip-spaced receiver and 25dB in a 3/4 chip-spaced receiver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel adaptive receiver for narrowband interference cancellation in CDMA systems which exploits the prior knowledge available about the interference.
the development of a new class of adaptive interference cancellation techniques for overlaid CDMA systems.

the development of a new narrowband interference cancellation algorithm that exploits the knowledge of the interference signal pulse shape and frequency in order to improve the performance of the cancellation process.

the adaptive narrowband interference cancellation technique described in this paper is a viable and attractive alternative to existing narrowband interference cancellation techniques in CDMA systems.
the proposed algorithm has a faster convergence rate and a better performance compared with the existing narrowband interference cancellation techniques.
the performance of a narrowband interference canceller can be improved significantly if prior information about the interference is used to design the canceller.

the adaptive narrowband interference cancellation algorithm is capable of achieving the same performance as the conventional narrowband interference cancellation techniques with less computational complexity, and is capable of achieving higher cancellation performance than the conventional techniques.
